title: Deprecate legacy batcher buffer and introduce epochal allocator
creator: Asha Raman
description: Background: The serving runtime still contains a legacy batcher buffer layer introduced early in the product that accumulates request fragments and applies ad-hoc memory reclamation. Over time this code has become brittle, hard to reason about and is the source of several tail-latency spikes under mixed workloads. Goal: Remove the legacy buffer, replace it with a deterministic epochal allocator and simplified lease model that cooperates with KV-cache lifecycle. This should reduce GC-like stalls, make prefetch semantics explicit, and make lease handoff deterministic for graceful model swaps.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy batcher buffer removed behind feature flag and gated rollout
End-to-end unit and integration tests covering lease handoff and allocator recovery
No increase in 99th percentile latency across canonical workloads (text-gen short/long & chat)
KV cache hit-rate stable or improved after rollout
Monitoring dashboards and alerts for allocator OOMs, lease disagreements and commit latency
design_notes: Introduce epoch id per allocation window; allocator reclaims only when all in-flight epochs are drained
Decouple allocation epoch from request sequence numbers to allow preemption (canary will set epoch-duration=50ms)
Simplify leases: single-lease per slot, explicit renewals from batch controller; remove implicit heartbeat-based promotion logic
Avoid global locks: allocator uses per-NUMA arenas with a light-weight epoch barrier for cross-arena GC
Compatibility shim: legacy buffer API implemented on top of epochal allocator for powering incremental rollout and migrations
migration_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement epochal allocator behind feature flag and add unit tests (PR #5123)
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for 10% of requests in staging, run perf harness for 48h
Phase 2 (region canary): enable for 5% of traffic in us-west-2 with continuous telemetry
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 24h soak between steps if metrics stable
Rollback: toggle feature flag off and fall back to legacy buffer; run automated rollback playbook
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator corner cases (cross-arena reclaim, double-free, delayed-drain)
Integration tests: end-to-end model swap with KV cache warmup and lease renewal under load
Perf harness: reproduce mixed short/long token mixes and compare p50/p95/p99 and tail latencies
Chaos tests: network partitions between scheduler and worker to validate lease expiry behavior
Load soak: 72h continuous run in staging with real traffic replay and memory profiling
monitoring: Alert: allocation_reclaim_latency > 200ms for 5m -> P0 alert to oncall
SLO watch: 99th latency must not increase by more than 5% vs baseline for 24h
Dashboards: KV cache hit-rate, lease renewal failures, allocator fragmentation ratio

2026-01-28 - Design sync: agreed to prefer epochal allocator with per-NUMA arenas. PM and Reliability approved trade-offs: slightly higher steady-state memory for lower tail latency.
2026-02-05 - Prototype: first-pass epochal allocator implemented; microbenchmarks show 12% reduction in p99 under synthetic mixed load (short+long tokens). Added feature flag 'allocator.v2'.
2026-02-12 - Review feedback: Security requested a clarifying comment about memory accounting for customer isolation (PR updated to include per-tenant metrics exposure but no data leak).

2026-02-28 - Code review: requested additional integration tests around lease preemption and race during model swap. Working on tests (ETA 2 days).
2026-03-05 - Blocker identified: one downstream component uses the legacy buffer's implicit reclaim semantics for a metric; added small compatibility shim and follow-up cleanup ticket ENG-305220.
